Independent lesson examples with 2017–2019 OUR/IM historical preparation source https://im.kendallhunt.com/MS/teachers/2/7/13/preparation.html (CC BY 4.0 attribution; no copied illustrations or assessments).

Use exact angle labels, defined length units, explicit geometric conditions and accessible diagrams or manipulatives when appropriate. Open constructions, counterexamples and peer explanations require teacher evaluation; numerical checks alone do not establish construction quality.

KeyConcepts.Title: Core geometric idea
KeyConcepts.Definition: A composite base can be split into nonoverlapping familiar shapes.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A composite base can be split into nonoverlapping familiar shapes.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rule and representation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Base area is sum of part areas.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Base area is sum of part areas.

KeyConcepts.Title: Verification
KeyConcepts.Definition: Prism volume is full base area times perpendicular height.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Prism volume is full base area times perpendicular height.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent geometric problem 1
WorkedExamples.Question: L-shaped base has rectangles 5×3 and 2×2 with no overlap. Area?
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the relevant geometric relation and verify all measurements and constraints.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use geometric invariants, substitution or physical construction evidence; teacher review for drawing quality.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent geometric problem 2
WorkedExamples.Question: The composite base area is 19 cm², height 6 cm. Volume?
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the relevant geometric relation and verify all measurements and constraints.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use geometric invariants, substitution or physical construction evidence; teacher review for drawing quality.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent geometric problem 3
WorkedExamples.Question: A 8×5 rectangle has a 2×3 cutout. Prism height 4. Volume?
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the relevant geometric relation and verify all measurements and constraints.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use geometric invariants, substitution or physical construction evidence; teacher review for drawing quality.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Overlapping decomposed pieces and counting the shared region twice.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It confuses geometric definition, measurement or construction condition.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check the relevant side, angle, base or dimensional units.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming a correct calculation guarantees a correct drawing or assembled solid
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The task also assesses an accurate representation and explicit construction constraints.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a diagram or physical model and teacher-reviewed geometric rubric.

SummaryPoints: A composite base can be split into nonoverlapping familiar shapes.
Base area is sum of part areas.
Prism volume is full base area times perpendicular height.

KeyConcepts.Definition: Surface area is total area of exposed faces.

KeyConcepts.Rule: A right prism has two congruent bases.

KeyConcepts.Rule: Lateral surface area for right prism=base perimeter×height.

KeyConcepts.Title: Core geometric idea
KeyConcepts.Definition: Volume has cubic units.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Volume has cubic units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rule and representation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Surface area has squared units.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Surface area has squared units.

KeyConcepts.Title: Verification
KeyConcepts.Definition: Scaling length by k scales volume by k³ but surface area by k².
KeyConcepts.Rule: Scaling length by k scales volume by k³ but surface area by k².

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent geometric problem 1
WorkedExamples.Question: Cube side 3 cm: volume and surface area?
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the relevant geometric relation and verify all measurements and constraints.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use geometric invariants, substitution or physical construction evidence; teacher review for drawing quality.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent geometric problem 2
WorkedExamples.Question: Cube side doubles 2→4. Compare volume factor.
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the relevant geometric relation and verify all measurements and constraints.
Steps: Compute 64÷8=8 as the ratio of new to original volume.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use geometric invariants, substitution or physical construction evidence; teacher review for drawing quality.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent geometric problem 3
WorkedExamples.Question: Same cube side doubles 2→4. Surface-area factor?
WorkedExamples.Method: Identify the relevant geometric relation and verify all measurements and constraints.
WorkedExamples.Check: Use geometric invariants, substitution or physical construction evidence; teacher review for drawing quality.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It confuses geometric definition, measurement or construction condition.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check the relevant side, angle, base or dimensional units.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming a correct calculation guarantees a correct drawing or assembled solid
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The task also assesses an accurate representation and explicit construction constraints.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a diagram or physical model and teacher-reviewed geometric rubric.

SummaryPoints: Volume has cubic units.
Surface area has squared units.
Scaling length by k scales volume by k³ but surface area by k².

KeyConcepts.Rule: A physical net requires bases and matching lateral rectangles.
